cards.text: Malachi, a prophet, brings the people a message: "You have wearied the LORD with your words" and they fire right back, "How have we wearied Him?" That's the friend who sends you FORTY texts in a row. Then comes the forty-first one: "You okay? You seem tired."

cards.question: The people ask how they've wearied the LORD with their words. What's one thing they've been saying?

answers.text: Evildoers are good in His sight
The prophets don't speak for Him

cards.text: Their other line is "Where is the God of justice?" I bet it's like me pressing my face on the oven door every ten seconds yelling WHERE ARE MY COOKIES.

cards.question: Then the LORD of Hosts speaks up. What does He say He will send?
The messenger the LORD sends will ___ the way before Him.

cards.text: Then the Lord they've been seeking will come to His temple, the one called the Messenger of the covenant. And the LORD of Hosts says, see, He is coming. That's the doorbell you've been waiting on ALL DAY, friend.

cards.question: The Lord the people are seeking will come to His temple slowly.
The LORD of Hosts calls the Messenger of the covenant someone the people delight in.

cards.text: They wanted Him to show up, and He's coming, but then the hard question hits: "But who can endure the day of His coming?" Be careful what you ask for, friend. You might GET it.

cards.question: The prophet asks who can stand when the Lord appears. Why will it be so hard?

answers.text: He'll be like a refiner's fire
He'll come with a great army
He'll shake the earth and sky

cards.question: The Lord will be like a refiner's fire and like a launderer's soap. What do fire and soap have in common here?

answers.text: They both are kept in the temple
They both get used up fast

cards.text: Then the prophet says He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver. SIT, friend, like He pulled up a chair for this one.

cards.question: The Lord sits like a refiner of silver. Who will He purify and refine like gold and silver?
After the Lord refines the sons of Levi, they will present offerings to the LORD in righteousness.
Once the refining is done, the offerings of ___ and ___ will please the LORD, just like in days gone by.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts says, "Then I will draw near to you for judgment." He'll be a witness against sorcerers, adulterers, perjurers and those who oppress the widowed and fatherless, and believe me, friend, this is NOT a list you want your name on.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts says He'll be a slow witness against these people and take His time.
The LORD names who He'll be a witness against. Which of these people is also on His list?

answers.text: Those who cheat workers of their wages
Those who skip the yearly feasts
Those who eat food that is unclean

cards.question: Last on the LORD's list: those who cheat workers of their wages and deny justice to the foreigner but do not ___ Him.

findings.problem: The card names Malachi as the prophet. Malachi isn't named anywhere in Malachi 2:17-3:5; that fact comes from Malachi 1:1. The card only cites Malachi 2:17, so the outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the Lord coming to His temple, the LORD of Hosts saying He is coming, and the doorbell joke. It isn't the opening card, so it can have only 1 or 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the setup with the quote, "Be careful what you ask for, friend." and "You might GET it." It isn't the opening card, so it can have only 1 or 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The punchline "Be careful what you ask for, friend. You might GET it." is a stock saying, not a real laugh. It reads like a nice dad being pleasant.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The question says "The prophet asks" for Malachi 3:2. The text doesn't say who speaks in 3:2: 3:1 ends with "says the LORD of Hosts" and 3:2 has no speaker tag. Naming the prophet fills in something the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Then the prophet says He will sit" names the prophet as the speaker of Malachi 3:3. The text doesn't say who speaks there.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "SIT, friend, like He pulled up a chair for this one" makes the joke about the Lord Himself. It pictures Him settling in to watch a show, which treats His refining work lightly.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: "a slow witness against these people" uses "these people" to point back to the list on story card 16. That card is no longer on screen, so the question doesn't say who is meant.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The two blanks, "offerings of ___ and ___", are a simple list, so "Jerusalem" then "Judah" means the same thing as "Judah" then "Jerusalem". The card only marks the BSB order as right, so a baker who picks the reverse order could argue they're right.
findings.question: When two blanks hold items in a list that could swap places without changing the meaning, should either order count as right, or should these cards be avoided or reworded so only one order makes sense?
